title: nOS entity — the base every organelle inherits
description:
The abstract nOS entity. It carries the harness every data node needs — compliance, access, cortex indexing, face rendering — as DATA, so a specific organelle inherits it by `allOf` instead of restating it. What may ACT on an entity is deliberately absent: `nos-cortex-lang.md` §2 and the Wing executor §2 both require that a capability must not be addable by data, so opcodes and handlers stay code, per runtime, hash-compared.

DIALECT: draft-07 with `definitions`, matching 6 of the 7 existing schemas in state/schema/. The estate already uses `$ref` 18 times — but every one is intra-file. Nothing here is a new idiom; this is the same factoring applied one level up, across a file boundary, which is the thing that has never been done.

EVIDENCE: the required core is not invented. All 72 plugin manifests declare name, version, description, type, requires and gdpr — measured, not assumed.

identity.description: Who this entity is. Empirically universal: 72/72 manifests carry all four.

name.description: Lower-kebab. Same charset as the agent-name rule in agent.schema.yaml, so one identifier style spans the estate.

kind.description: Which organelle this is. Open on purpose: the base must not need editing to admit a new kind.

anchor.description:
Cortex node this entity hangs from — an id from the committed 362-anchor spine (state/fable/taxonomy-bundle.json `anchor`), e.g. `02.02.11`. What makes `ent:` addressable from cortex-lang once the registry lands (cortex-self-core.md §6b).

RENAMED from `taxonomy_anchor` on 2026-08-07, and the rename IS the finding. Measured: `taxonomy_anchor` had zero producers and zero consumers for its whole life (one grep, one hit — its own declaration), while 196 anatomy-graph nodes carried the same fact under the name `anchor`, and its example spelling `tax:02.02.11` matched none of the 362 live ids. One fact, two names, the dead one in the genome — which is the exact defect this file exists to end, so it is repaired rather than aliased.

OPTIONAL, not required, and the asymmetry is deliberate: 196/196 graph nodes carry one, 0/1 organelle instances do. The pattern is generated into both runtimes as ANCHOR_PATTERN so a dangling anchor is refused at compile time by whatever stamps it — `tools/anatomy-graph-gen.py` refuses one that fails this pattern, and `tests/anatomy/test_anatomy_graph_is_sound.py` separately refuses one the spine does not hold. Shape and membership are two checks because a well-formed id that names nothing is the failure this estate actually hits.

compliance.description: GDPR Article 30 register row. ONE spelling — this supersedes the split between plugin.schema.json (5 required keys, `eu_residency`) and app.schema.json (7 required, `transfers_outside_eu`), which is the divergence `nos_gdpr.py` exists to paper over.

retention_days.description: Days. 0 = stores nothing itself (the horizon is owned by whatever it wires into). -1 = indefinite / no automatic horizon — 12 manifests use it and plugin.schema.json already allows it, so the genome does too. A schema that rejected live values would be a redesign wearing a schema's clothes.

eu_residency.description: CANONICAL residency field, and intended to become required. NOT required yet: 3 of 72 manifests (hermes-base, openclaw-base, vaultwarden-base) declare residency ONLY via the deprecated inverse `transfers_outside_eu: false`. That is a rename to make, not missing data — which is exactly the kind of distinction the split spelling was hiding. test_genome_contract.py pins the list so it can only shrink.

transfers_outside_eu.description: DEPRECATED alias — the logical inverse of eu_residency. Retained so the 22 manifests that carry it keep validating; consistency between the two is asserted by the validator, not expressible here. New entities declare eu_residency only.

access.description: Reachability and gating as ONE fact. Today this is split across five uncoordinated declarations — state/manifest.yml (a router exists), traefik_auth_modes (what attaches), traefik_skip_ids (whether to route), the plugin's authentik block (whether a provider exists to attach), and authentik_app_tiers (who may pass). Nothing compares them, and for `traefik` they disagreed: that is REM-144, a publicly reachable API whose only justification was a prose comment that had been false for three months.

routed.description: Whether an edge router is rendered for this entity at all.

gate.description: What stands in front of it. Mirrors the SSO trichotomy in CLAUDE.md plus the ungated case.

justification.description: Why an ungated route is acceptable. A FIELD, not a comment — the whole point of REM-144 is that a comment cannot be checked and rots silently.

tier.description: RBAC tier: 1 admin, 2 manager, 3 user, 4 guest.

then.description: A routed entity with no gate is anonymously reachable. It must say why, in a field a test can read. This clause IS the REM-144 gate, expressed as schema instead of as a hand-written pytest.

cortex.description: How the knowledge layer sees this entity.

indexed.description: Whether the entity is materialised as a cortex object (and therefore embedded, searchable, and visible in /explore).

body_fields.description: Which fields form the embedded body. Order is significant — it is what the router answers from.

excluded_fields.description: Fields that must never reach an embedding or an index. This is where the boolean the first draft wanted to bolt on actually belongs: as one facet field, scoped, rather than a loose column flag.

face.description: Render hints for the web desktop. Today these are scattered across hub_card, table defs and Wing columns, hand-mirrored between face and KEAP with no gate — and already drifted (face has 11 ColumnKinds to KEAP's 12).

axes.description:
The adjectives. `form` (what a thing IS on screen), `build` (what it COST to build), `layer` (where it SITS in the dependency arithmetic) — one facet, three axes, deliberately.

WHY ONE FACET. Before 2026-08-07 these were three parallel registries with nothing between them: `form` and `build` as TypeScript unions in files/anatomy/face/src/lib/contracts/index.ts, `layer` as four string literals inside tools/anatomy-graph-gen.py::derive_layers plus prose in docs/doctrine/layers.md §3, and the anatomy compiler validating NONE of the three — a typo'd `form: 'veiw'` in the face registry compiled into the address space as a fourth form and no gate could tell. Three axes, three declarations, zero comparison. That is the shape the genome exists to collapse, one level up from where it has already collapsed compliance and access.

`additionalProperties: false` IS the rule the doc asks for: a fourth adjective cannot be added by inventing a fifth file, because an entity carrying one fails validation until the axis is declared HERE and generated into every runtime by the same emitter. The artifact-side twin of that clause is the generated `AXES` tuple, which tools/anatomy-graph-gen.py::stamp_axes refuses to write outside of.

WHAT IS NOT HERE. `tier` (RBAC) lives in `access` and keeps its one surviving meaning; delivery tier is retired. Neither is an adjective about the thing itself — one is a permission, one was a shipping route.

form.description: What a face app IS on screen. Exactly one per app, always declared, never inferred. Replaced a boolean (`isNativeApp`, plus a dead `HubApp.native`) that could only answer 'component or iframe' and had nothing to say about a widget — native AND not a window. `utility` is an EMPTY SET today (docs/doctrine/face-app-tiers.md names Sticky Notes as its reference and no such app exists in this shell); a zero here is a measurement, not a slot to fill with a token app.

build.description: What a face app COST to build — which organs and which agent recipe (docs/doctrine/face-app-tiers.md owns the axis and keeps its prefixes). INDEPENDENT of `form` and only loosely correlated: a frame is usually cheapest and a view usually is not, but that is a tendency, not a definition, and the field that conflated them was wrong about both. Nothing derives either axis from the other.

layer.description: Where a service SITS: L0 substrate · L1 platform · L2 application · L3 custom (docs/doctrine/layers.md §3). DERIVED — longest path over the service projection of the dependency edges — never declared. `layer:` in a plugin manifest or in state/manifest.yml is a gate failure (test_service_layer_is_derived.py). `null` is a first-class value, not a missing one: it means the estate refuses to place this service, and the clause below makes it say why. L3 is in the enum because §3 defines it, and is never emitted, because §3 defines it by DELIVERY — a different axis wearing this one's name.

layer_withheld.description: Why no layer was derived. A FIELD, not an omission — the same shape as `access.justification`, for the same reason: 38 of 63 services are unplaced today, and an absent `layer` that rendered as a default would make 'we have not read this role' indistinguishable from 'this is an application leaf'. Measured with the refusal off, service:traefik derives L2 and service:grafana derives L0 from the identical absence of evidence.

layer_basis.description: The arithmetic that produced the layer, published beside it. A derived value that does not carry its derivation is an assertion.

height.description: Longest path from this node to a leaf of the service projection.

then.description: A withheld layer must state its reason. This clause is the REM-144 clause pointed at absence instead of at exposure: an unmeasured value gets its own visible state, never a default that looks fine.
A placed service publishes its arithmetic and withholds nothing. Carrying both a layer and a withholding reason is two answers to one question.

entity.description: The base. An organelle composes this with `allOf` and adds its own kind-specific properties.

llm.description:
A VOCABULARY, not a facet — which is why it lives beside `definitions` rather than inside it. A facet is something an ENTITY carries; nOS services do not have an `llm` block, and `test_every_facet_is_reachable_from_the_base` was right to refuse it as one on the first run. Vocabularies are shared closed lists the runtimes agree on; they are emitted by the codegen and composed into nothing.

Which model may be NAMED, and in what spelling. NOT which model an agent may USE — that is a capability and stays hand-written per runtime, the same split this file's own description draws for opcodes.

WHY IT IS HERE. Measured 2026-08-10: the identical alternation `(anthropic|openclaw|openai|local)` was restated SIX times — AgentLoader.php:261, state/schema/agent.schema.yaml three times (primary, fallback, and the grader's), tests/anatomy/test_agentkit_naming.py, and cortex's MODEL_URI_RE in two vendored copies. The sixth was written the day before this facet and ALREADY DISAGREED with the other five on the tail, which is how fast this drifts when nothing compares it.

WHY THE TAIL IS PERMISSIVE, and it is the whole reason the drift mattered. The old tail was `[a-z0-9.-]+` — no colon. Every real ollama tag has one (`qwen2.5-coder:32b`, `nomic-embed-text:latest`, `hermes3:8b` on this host), so the correct value was UNWRITEABLE and got dash-ified into `qwen-coder-32b`, a model that does not exist, as the fallback of all nine agents. We own the provider prefix; the vendor owns everything after it, which is what docs/doctrine/foreign-properties.md asks of us.

provider.description:
FAIL-CLOSED ORDERING, inherited verbatim from the opcode/handler rule: the ADAPTER ships first and the provider joins this enum second. A member here with no adapter is a URI the schema accepts and the Factory throws on — validation that outruns capability. `minimax` is deliberately ABSENT until its adapter exists.

NARROWED 2026-08-10 BY THIS RULE'S FIRST RUN, which is the useful part: `openai` and `local` were in the list and Factory::fromUri has no arm for either — its own docstring calls them 'reserved (not yet implemented; throws)'. So an agent.yml declaring `primary: openai-gpt-4` passed every schema check in the estate and failed at session-open. Reserved belongs in the CODE, where the Factory already says so, not in the vocabulary a validator accepts. Nothing used either (checked across agents/, apps/ and plugins/), so narrowing cost nothing and closed a gap the gate was written to find in someone else's declaration.

`claude` ADDED 2026-08-11, and only after `ClaudeCliAdapter` existed — this list's own rule is that the enum ships SECOND, because a member with no adapter is validation outrunning the runtime. It names the LOCAL `claude` binary, not the API: the eight nightly ceremonies run on the operator's subscription through pulse-run-agent.sh, and until this entry every one of the nine agent profiles declared `anthropic-claude-opus-4-7` — a backend needing an API key the estate does not set. Nine profiles naming a runtime that could not run them, validated by a list that permitted nothing else.

model_id_pattern.description: The tail after `<provider>-`. Another system's identifier, carried unedited: dots, colons, slashes and underscores all appear in real registries. Bounded at 96 so it cannot be an injection surface.
